# Known gaps

Rules from Weiss Schwarz (English Edition) Comprehensive Rules v2.10 that v1 of the engine does not implement.
Cards whose text depends on these rules cannot be played as written. The in-app Help screen shows this same list.

59 deferred rules.

## GEN: Player count and golden rules (CR 1.1, 1.3)

- **GEN-02** (§1.3.1): Where a card's text and the comprehensive rules disagree, the card's text governs. _Only testable once card abilities exist (M3), but M1 rule checks (hand limit, play restrictions, costs, etc.) should be built so effects can override them. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effects that change or override a rule._
- **GEN-03** (§1.3.1.1): If the English Edition and Japanese Edition text of a card conflict, each player is governed by the card text in their own language edition. _English-vs-Japanese text conflicts are deferred; v1 uses a single canonical text per card._
- **GEN-07** (§1.3.3): When one card effect tries to perform an action while another card effect at the same time prevents that action, the preventing effect wins. _Prohibition effects must be checked before any action an effect attempts. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no prohibition effects._
- **GEN-09** (§1.3.5): When a player must pick a number, it must be zero or a positive whole number unless stated otherwise; fractions and negative values are not allowed. _No M1 rule asks a player to choose a number; numeric choices arrive with card effects in M3. Validate all numeric choices as non-negative integers by default. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that asks a player for a number._

## WIN: Winning, losing, draws, conceding (CR 1.2)

- **WIN-07** (§1.2.4.1): Card effects cannot prevent or interfere with a concession, cannot compel a player to concede, and cannot turn a game loss into a concession. _Concede handling must bypass all effect hooks. The 'replace a loss with a concession' clause concerns replacement effects, which are deferred in v1. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that concedes, wins or loses, or interferes with conceding._
- **WIN-08** (§1.2.5): When a card effect makes a player win or lose, that result happens during the effect's resolution and the game ends right then, without waiting for a check timing. _Unlike losing conditions (WIN-02), no rule-action pass is needed. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that makes a player win or lose._

## CARD: Card information (CR 2)

- **CARD-04** (§2.1.2.1, §2.1.2.2): Text of the form 'with "X" in its card name' matches cards whose name contains X as a portion: the bilingual form matches a part of the English name together with a part of the Japanese name, and the English-only form requires X to be bounded on each side by a punctuation mark or by nothing (start/end of the name). _Card-name partial matching is deferred. Illustration with invented names: "ORB" matches "Kael: Keeper of ORB", "ORB: Last Light" and "Mira \"ORB\" Vance", but not "Orbital" (a space counts as a valid boundary)._
- **CARD-15** (§2.8.3): A card with the Clock icon has an ability that is relevant while the card is in the clock. _Clock icon is deferred in v1._
- **CARD-22** (§2.19.2): When two non-numeric values are compared and at least one of them is missing, they are never treated as identical. _Matters for effects comparing names/traits; e.g., two cards with no traits do not 'share' a trait. Deferred in M3: v1 filters compare card information only against fixed values, never two cards against each other._

## ZONE: Zones of the game (CR 3)

- **ZONE-24** (§3.7.1.1, §3.7.1.2, §3.7.4): Each stage position has its own marker area, which has the same positional relations as that position (center/back, left/middle/right, in front, behind, facing) but is a separate zone that is not on the stage; a character whose marker area holds cards is a 'character with marker(s)'. _Marker area is deferred in v1._
- **ZONE-25** (§3.7.2, §3.7.2.1, §3.7.2.1.1, §3.7.2.2): The marker area is hidden: by default its cards are face down and no one may see their information or order or reorder them; cards are added on top (in any order if several at once) and removed from the top in order. Some effects place markers face up, which all players may then see, and when a face-up marker is exchanged with a face-up card on the stage, both stay face up after the swap. _Marker area is deferred in v1._
- **ZONE-26** (§3.7.3, §3.7.3.1, §3.7.3.2): Markers travel with their character: if it moves to another stage position of the same master, its markers move with it and any markers already in the destination marker area go to their owner's waiting room; if it moves to any non-stage-position zone, its markers go to their owner's waiting room at the same time. _Marker area is deferred in v1. Orphaned markers are cleaned up by rule action 9.7._
- **ZONE-30** (§3.9.2.2, §3.9.2.2.1, §3.9.2.2.2): Unless stated otherwise, face-down cards in the level are visible only to their owner and count as blank cards with no information; when one moves to another zone it is placed face up or face down according to the destination, and its information is not revealed if it moves to a hidden zone. _Face-down level cards are deferred in v1._
- **ZONE-34** (§3.12.1, §3.12.2, §3.12.2.1, §3.12.2.3): The memory is a zone cards enter only when explicitly instructed; it is public, its cards are face up unless stated otherwise and viewable by all, and a player may reorder the face-up cards in their own memory. Cards there may be called simply 'memory'. _Memory zone mechanics are deferred in v1._
- **ZONE-35** (§3.12.2.2, §3.12.2.2.1, §3.12.2.2.2, §3.12.2.2.3): Unless stated otherwise, face-down cards in memory are visible only to their owner, must be kept so the order they were placed face down is clear, and count as blank unless their ability explicitly works face down there; when moved they are placed face up or down according to the destination without revealing information if it is hidden, and when shuffled by an effect no player may see them unless the effect says they may be seen or revealed. _Memory zone mechanics are deferred in v1._
- **ZONE-40** (§3.13.1.4): Cards placed in the resolution zone by a Brainstorm ability sit there temporarily and then go to their owner's waiting room. _Brainstorm keyword (10.7) is deferred in v1._

## CONC: Basic concepts (CR 4.1-4.9)

- **CONC-03** (§4.1.2.1): Replacement effects form a third, separate category of effects. _Replacement effects are on the v1 deferral list; cards that depend on them are not supported in v1._
- **CONC-18** (§4.9.1): An instruction to reveal the top N cards of the deck, or up to N cards from the top, shows those cards' information openly while the cards stay in the deck. _No zone change; the revealed cards' information is displayed, unlike looking (CONC-17). Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no reveal effect (looking is supported: CONC-17)._

## DMG: Damage process and source of damage (CR 4.10-4.11)

- **DMG-05** (§4.10.3): A general reference in an effect to cards moved into a zone or revealed by an effect excludes cards handled during a Damage Process; only an effect that names damage specifically counts those cards. _Tag zone moves and reveals with whether they came from a Damage Process so that effect queries can include or exclude them. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that refers to cards moved or revealed by an effect. Applies to references to moved or revealed cards, not to counts of what is in a zone._

## TRG: Trigger icons (CR 4.12)

- **TRG-09** (§4.12.2.7.2): Shot's trigger condition is not limited to damage aimed at the opponent: if the attacking character's next damage is dealt to its own player and is canceled, Shot still fires. _Self-damage only comes from effects, so this case can only be tested once M3 lands. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no self-damage from the attacking character's own ability._
- **TRG-10** (§4.12.2.7.1): Shot watches only the attacking character's first damage after the trigger. If the character deals damage before the Damage Step and that damage is canceled, Shot fires; if that earlier damage is not canceled, Shot is used up and a cancel in the Damage Step does not fire it. _Bind Shot to the next damage event, not to Damage Step damage. Damage before the Damage Step only comes from abilities, so this can only be tested once M3 lands. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no way for the attacker to deal damage after its trigger check and before the Damage Step ("when this attacks" abilities resolve before the Trigger Step)._
- **TRG-11** (§4.12.2.7.3): If the attacking character's next damage is dealt to several players at once, a cancel against any of them fires Shot, and Shot fires only once even if damage to more than one player is canceled. _Damage to several players at once only comes from effects, so this can only be tested once M3 lands. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no damage to several players at once. When added, Shot must settle the simultaneous damage as one event, not one damage process at a time._

## DECK: Deck construction (CR 5.1)

- **DECK-04** (§5.1.2.4): If a card has a continuous ability about deck construction, that card's text replaces the standard deck construction rules to the extent it specifies. _The M1 validator should leave room for per-card overrides; until continuous abilities exist, apply the defaults. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no deck-construction abilities._

## TSTEP: Trigger step (CR 7.3)

- **TSTEP-05** (§7.3.1.2.3.1): Card text about 'this card's trigger check' means the trigger checks made for this card's attack. 'Your character's trigger check' means the trigger checks made for attacks by your characters. _Each trigger check must be linked to the attacker it was made for. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that refers to trigger checks._

## ABL: Abilities, effects and timing (CR 8.1-8.3, 8.5, 8.7-8.12)

- **ABL-02** (§8.1.1.1.2): A trigger worded 'when (player) uses an activated ability' is met at the instant that player completes payment of that ability's cost. _The triggered ability then waits in standby until the next check timing (ABL-10). Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no "when (player) uses an activated ability" triggers._
- **ABL-13** (§8.7.4, §8.7.4.1, §8.7.4.1.1, §8.7.4.1.2, §8.7.4.1.3): When a zone-change triggered ability needs the moved card's information: a move between a public and a hidden zone uses the card's public-zone information; a move off the stage, or any move that changes its master, uses its on-stage information; any other public-to-public move uses its information in the destination zone. _Snapshot card information at move time and attach it to the standby instance (e.g. a character going stage to waiting room reports its on-stage power and traits). Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no zone-change trigger that reads the moved card's information._
- **ABL-14** (§8.7.5, §8.7.5.1): An automatic ability created by an effect to trigger at some later moment (a timed trigger) has its trigger met only once, unless the effect says otherwise. _Remove the delayed trigger after its first firing by default. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no timed (delayed) triggers created by effects. Shot is the rule-level case and fires once by construction._
- **ABL-15** (§8.7.6, §8.7.6.1): A state trigger (met by a condition being true rather than by an event) enters standby only one time when its condition is fulfilled; after that ability resolves, it enters standby again if the condition is still fulfilled. _Do not re-queue while the instance is pending. State triggers can repeat indefinitely; infinite-loop handling (11.1) is deferred. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no state triggers._
- **ABL-17** (§8.9.1, §8.9.1.1, §8.9.1.2, §8.9.1.3): To compute a card's information under continuous effects, begin with what is printed on the card, next apply every continuous effect that leaves the value itself unchanged, and only then apply every continuous effect that alters the value. _CR example: a conditional '+500 if power is 3000 or less' on a 3000 character yields 3500 and is not then switched off by the boosted value. The CR does not list which effect types fall in each layer; classify per effect type. Deferred in M3: every v1 modifier adds to power or soul; none grants abilities or traits or depends on the value it changes, so layer order never shows._
- **ABL-18** (§8.9.1.4): When two continuous effects are not ordered by the layer rule and applying effect A changes what effect B applies to or how it applies, B depends on A and is always applied after A, regardless of which was created first. _CR example: one Assist grants a trait and another grants Encore to characters with that trait; the front character gets the Encore whatever the placement order. Deferred in M3: no v1 effect changes what another effect applies to (no trait or ability grants)._
- **ABL-19** (§8.9.1.5, §8.9.1.5.1, §8.9.1.5.2): Continuous effects still unordered after layers and dependency apply in creation order: an effect from a continuous ability is timestamped when its card arrived in its current zone (for a character on stage, when it was put onto its current stage position from another zone), and an effect from any other ability is timestamped when that ability was played. _CR example: Assist +500 followed by an event setting power to 0 until end of turn gives 0. Whether swapping stage positions resets a character's timestamp is not explicit; the text keys it to arrival from another zone. Deferred in M3: every v1 modifier adds, and addition gives the same result in any order. Needs a decision on whether a stage-position swap resets the timestamp once set-value effects exist._
- **ABL-22** (§8.9.3.1): When an automatic ability triggers on a card with given information entering a given zone, that card's information is read only after the continuous effects of that zone have been applied to it. _Apply zone modifiers before evaluating entry triggers. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no entry trigger that reads the entering card's information._
- **ABL-23** (§8.2.1.3.1, §8.2.1.3.2, §8.10.1, §8.10.1.1, §8.10.2, §8.10.2.1, §8.10.2.2, §8.10.2.3, §8.10.2.4, §8.10.3): A replacement effect ('if X would do A, do B instead', optionally with 'may') stops the original event from happening at all and substitutes the new one; when several apply to the same event, the affected player (card or ability master, or the acting player / applying card's master for game actions) chooses the order, each applies at most once, attack-type replacements apply turn player's first, and an optional replacement whose choice cannot be made is not applied. _Replacement effects are out of v1 scope. The attack-type ordering mainly interacts with Great Performance (10.6), also deferred._
- **ABL-24** (§8.11.1): If an effect refers to a specific card's information or state and that card moves to another zone while the effect is being carried out (moves between stage positions excepted), the effect uses the card's last known information and state from the zone it left. _Keep a last-known-information snapshot for cards leaving a zone mid-effect. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no effect that moves a card and then refers to it._
- **ABL-25** (§8.11.2): If a battling character moves zones or stage positions after an automatic ability triggered but before that ability resolves, the effect still treats the two characters as having been battle opponents, using that as final information. _Store the battle-opponent pairing in the trigger context instead of re-deriving it from current positions. Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no battle-opponent references._
- **ABL-26** (§8.12.1): A Climax Combo icon following an Ability Category Icon only marks an ability linked to a climax with a given name; the icon itself has no rules meaning. _Climax Combo icon handling is deferred; the linked ability's own text still governs._

## COST: Costs (CR 8.4)

- **COST-02** (§8.4.2.1, §9.2.3, §9.3.3): Between the start and the end of paying a cost, neither refresh nor level up is carried out. _Card play costs (stock) cannot empty the deck or fill the clock, so this only bites with ability costs. The CR states only the prohibition; presumably the interrupt runs once payment ends if its condition still holds. Deferred in M3: no v1 cost moves cards from the deck or into the clock, and every cost is paid inside one engine step anyway._

## ILL: Illegal cards and unaffiliated markers (CR 9.6-9.7)

- **ILL-03** (§9.7.1): If a marker area contains cards while its matching stage position has no character, all of those cards go to their respective owners' waiting rooms as a check-type rule action. _Marker area is deferred._

## KW: Keywords and keyword abilities (CR 10)

- **KW-01** (§10.1.1, §10.1.2): Alarm is a keyword label for abilities that grant an ability, or let a trigger condition be met, while the card is the top card of its owner's clock; the keyword itself has no effect.
- **KW-04** (§10.2.4): A 'when (player) uses this card's Encore' trigger is met when that character is put onto the stage from the waiting room by an Encore effect. _Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no "when this card's Encore is used" triggers._
- **KW-05** (§10.3.1, §10.3.2): Assist is a continuous keyword ability: the text after it is an active effect only while the character is on the back stage. _Uses the active/inactive mechanism of ABL-06._
- **KW-06** (§10.4.1, §10.4.2, §10.4.2.1): Bond/'Name' [cost] is an automatic ability: when this character is played and placed on stage, or placed on stage from hand, its master may pay the cost to return a card with that name from their waiting room to hand; if several names are listed, a card matching any one of them may be chosen.
- **KW-09** (§10.5.3): A 'when (player) uses Backup' trigger is met once that player finishes paying the cost of a Backup ability. _Deferred in M3: the v1 ability language has no "when you use Backup" triggers._
- **KW-10** (§10.6.1, §10.6.2): Great Performance: while this character is in the middle position of its master's center stage and is not Reversed, any attack by an opposing character becomes a frontal attack against this character as though it were the defending character. _Acts as an attack-type replacement; see ABL-23 for ordering._
- **KW-11** (§10.7.1, §10.7.2, §10.7.3, §10.7.4): Brainstorm labels effects that flip a set number of cards off the top of the deck into the waiting room and check their information; the flipped cards all go to the resolution zone first and then move to the waiting room together, and 'uses Brainstorm' means the moment they land in the waiting room.
- **KW-12** (§10.8.1, §10.8.2, §10.8.3, §10.8.4, §10.8.5): Change labels abilities that either, when the Change character goes to a specified zone, bring a specified character from that zone into the Change character's former zone, or exchange the Change character with a specified character in a specified zone; the exchange is not done if, during resolution, the Change character changed zones (stage-position moves aside) or the specified card is not in that zone. 'Uses Change' and 'placed on the stage by a Change effect' refer to a character being put onto the stage by such an effect.
- **KW-13** (§10.9.1, §10.9.2): Memory labels abilities that count cards (etc.) in the memory zone or that work while the card is in memory; the keyword itself has no effect. _Memory zone mechanics are deferred._
- **KW-14** (§10.10.1, §10.10.2): Experience labels abilities that count cards (etc.) in the level zone or that work while the card is in the level zone; the keyword itself has no effect.
- **KW-15** (§10.11.1, §10.11.2, §10.11.3, §10.11.3.1, §10.11.3.2, §10.11.4): Shift, Level N: at the start of its master's main phase, if this card is in clock and their level is N or higher, they may swap it with a same-colored card from hand; exactly those two cards must be chosen, and no swap is allowed if this card cannot be chosen or there is no same-colored card in hand.
- **KW-16** (§10.12.1, §10.12.2, §10.12.3): Accelerate labels abilities whose cost includes putting a card into the clock; 'uses Accelerate' means finishing payment of that cost.
- **KW-17** (§10.13.1, §10.13.2, §10.13.3, §10.13.3.1, §10.13.3.2): Resonate labels cards or abilities that reveal a specified card from hand in their cost or effect; it counts as used when that reveal cost is paid, or, when the reveal is not a cost, when the 'you may reveal' cards are revealed as specified.
- **KW-18** (§10.14.1, §10.14.1.1, §10.14.1.1.1, §10.14.1.1.2, §10.14.1.1.2.1, §10.14.2, §10.14.3): Fusion labels activated abilities that put this character and another specified character as markers under a character searched from the deck and placed on this card's position; if that character is not placed, the effect stops with the cost character left as a marker of the Fusion character and the deck still shuffled. _Existing markers of the Fusion character carry over to the new one; markers of the cost character go to the waiting room when the cost is paid._
- **KW-19** (§10.15.1, §10.15.2, §10.15.3, §10.15.3.1, §10.15.4): Sunder: at the end of this character's attack, its master may pay the cost to put a named marker from under it onto a chosen stage position as a new character (in Stand State unless stated), with this card and the other markers under it; if no such named marker exists when the cost is paid, nothing further happens. _The new character carries over none of the effects or statuses of the Sunder character._
- **KW-20** (§10.16.1, §10.16.2, §10.16.3, §10.16.4, §10.16.4.1): Link (Name) is a continuous ability that only names something; it has no effect of its own, but other effects can refer to cards 'with' that Link name.
- **KW-21** (§10.17.1, §10.17.2, §10.17.2.1, §10.17.3, §10.17.4): An activated or automatic ability marked N/Turn cannot be played once it has been played N times this turn; while under that limit, a standby automatic ability with this restriction may be either played or have one standby instance discarded unplayed. _Exception to mandatory play of standby abilities (ABL-11)._

## MISC: Miscellaneous (CR 11)

- **MISC-01** (§11.1.1, §11.1.1.1, §11.1.1.2, §11.1.1.3): In an infinite loop that neither player can stop the game is a draw; if one player can stop it they declare a repeat count, run it that many times, and stop it, and if both can, turn player then opponent declare counts and the lower declarer runs and stops it. Afterward, if the game state is exactly unchanged, the loop may not be chosen again (only by the higher declarer when both could stop it), except when forced by automatic abilities and the like.
- **MISC-02** (§11.2.1, §11.2.2): An effect granting an additional turn makes the named player the next turn player when play passes from the End Phase to a new turn; if several such effects exist, the turn player applies one of the most recently generated and the rest wait until the following turn.
- **MISC-03** (§11.3.1, §11.3.1.1, §11.3.1.2, §11.3.1.3, §11.3.2): A Replay Command (green-bordered text with a Replay Icon) has its Replay Effect carried out only when the card's own effect resolves the red text naming its Replay Action; nothing else can make the Replay Command happen.
- **MISC-04** (§11.4.1, §11.4.1.1, §11.4.1.2, §11.4.1.3): When an effect jumps play to a named phase or step, continuous effects due to expire in between end, the intervening phases/steps and their check timings are skipped along with anything that would have happened in them, and pending check-type rule actions and standby automatic abilities are handled at the check timing of the destination phase or step.
